teaser: Cloudflare's developer platform as the smallest free blocks a non-specialist can use, and an sgit vault on it: no code read-only, 83 lines read-write.
core_idea: Cloudflare's platform maps to small free blocks a non-specialist can assemble once with an agent; Workers AI keeps @cf models inside the account without training on content; an sgit vault needs no code read-only and an 83-line Worker read-write, tested with the real client; and the setup must be a button, a temporary account or an agent because the API cannot be called from a page.

figures.caption: Cloudflare's developer platform as blocks, grouped by job. Put something on the web: static assets, free and unlimited; Workers, 100,000 requests a day; DNS and domains at cost. Keep data: R2 with 10 GB and zero egress, D1, KV, Durable Objects. Think with models it hosts: Workers AI with 10,000 neurons a day on Cloudflare's own GPUs, AI Gateway, Vectorize and AI Search. Run jobs: cron, queues and workflows, Browser Run, and Containers on the paid plan. Talk and guard: inbound email routing, email sending on the paid plan, Access free to 50 users, Turnstile and Tunnel.
medium
figures.kind: Two ways to put an sgit vault on Cloudflare, both tested on 18 October 2026 with the real sgit client. Read-only: sgit publish writes the plaintext cover and a manifest, with the encrypted objects beside them; any static host serves it, and sgit clone with the read key and the static transport cloned it back identically. Read-write: a Worker of 83 lines, R2 for the encrypted objects, and a Durable Object per vault that runs writes one at a time; tested for push, clone, a stale push, two pushes at once, a read-only clone and a wrong write key, with no plaintext in the server's storage.
